# unsurf | unsurf

Source: https://unsurf.coey.dev/

Parallel discovery

Several causal investigators explore a vague symptom in independent browser surfaces.

Unsurf discovers a browser repro, promotes only observed behavior, and independently confirms the fix.

**Ultimate dogfood:** Unsurf recorded its own updated production documentation.

Parallel discovery

Several causal investigators explore a vague symptom in independent browser surfaces.

Fresh confirmation

Only an observed candidate is replayed three times against broken and fixed targets.

Portable repro

`repro.json` is the deterministic contract. Model prose is never confirmation.

Evidence-backed

Every run emits screenshots, state timelines, a machine receipt, and a reviewer report.

Authenticated browser

cmux uses the real browser profile you already trust. Provider isolation is always explicit.

Hosted execution

Browser Run remains the isolated hosted lane with native replay recordings.

Reproducibility is mandatory. Video is optional evidence determined by provider capabilities.

# Investigate and confirm browser bugs | unsurf

Source: https://unsurf.coey.dev/guides/investigate/

# Investigate and confirm browser bugs

Unsurf can open several investigators in the browser you already trust, promote only an observed reproduction path, and replay it against broken and fixed targets.

Dogfood receipt:this video was captured with Unsurf’s local video-capable provider after deploying this guide. The guide documents why reproducibility is mandatory while video remains capability-driven evidence.

The local provider uses cmux’s in-app browser. It supports authenticated interaction, snapshots, and screenshots. cmux surfaces share the Default browser profile, so a fresh surface is not automatically a fresh browser identity.

Unsurf will:

- run four causal investigators in separate cmux surfaces;
- promote only a path that observes the unwanted state;
- replay that path three times against the broken target;
- replay it three times against the fixed target;
- write a portable repro, screenshots, machine receipt, and reviewer report.

Typical output:

`repro.json` is the contract. Model prose is never treated as confirmation.

The default fixture convention reads `body[data-state]` and treats `resumed` as failure. For another app:

Reproducibility is mandatory. Video is optional evidence.

The cmux provider produces action timelines, snapshots, state assertions, and screenshots. Providers with recording support may also attach video or session replay. Unsurf never invents artifacts a provider cannot capture.

---

# Record a browser session | unsurf

Source: https://unsurf.coey.dev/guides/record/

# Record a browser session

`record` is Unsurf’s video-capable proof layer. It wraps a supported browser run and produces a video, trace, status bundle, and viewer link.

## Start from a real browser for video capture

[Section titled “Start from a real browser for video capture”](https://unsurf.coey.dev#start-from-a-real-browser-for-video-capture)

Sign in once. Reuse that browser for video-capable agent work. For normal authenticated investigation, sign in directly through cmux instead.

## Record the browser already open on your machine

[Section titled “Record the browser already open on your machine”](https://unsurf.coey.dev#record-the-browser-already-open-on-your-machine)

CLI equivalent:

Browser Run is the hosted/provider lane: Cloudflare Worker-side browser flows with the same browser-handle verbs.

`recordBrowserRunSession(...)` turns on Browser Run’s native session recording and returns its session ID after the session closes. Browser Run recordings are replayable rrweb events in Browser Run logs/API, not MP4 files. Local attached Chrome remains the playable-video path.

- run status
- trace id
- viewer URL
- optional signed video URL
- metadata for the task and provider

Every new trace is grant-gated by default. See [Privacy](https://unsurf.coey.dev/guides/privacy/).

Record when:

- a browser task should be reviewable later
- an agent run should produce proof, not just text logs
- you want a video suitable for docs, debugging, or sharing

# MCP Server | unsurf

Source: https://unsurf.coey.dev/guides/mcp/

# MCP Server

The unsurf MCP server is available at:

It uses the **Streamable HTTP** transport from the [MCP specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io). The server runs in stateless mode — each request is independent.

For full documentation of all tool inputs, outputs, and error types, see the [MCP Tools reference](https://unsurf.coey.dev/reference/tools).

Add this to your Claude Desktop MCP config (`~/.claude/mcp.json`):

Restart Claude Desktop. You should see **unsurf** listed under the MCP tools icon.

Open Cursor Settings → MCP Servers → **Add Server** and enter:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | `unsurf` |
| Transport | `Streamable HTTP` |
| URL | `https://unsurf-api.coey.dev/mcp` |

Cursor will discover the available tools automatically.

Use the hosted MCP server for Cloudflare-side scout/search/plan work. Use the local stdio server when an agent should operate the Chrome session already open on your machine:

The local server exposes two tools:

- `unsurf_local_sessions`— list attachable local Chrome/CDP tabs
- `unsurf_local_execute`— run small browser action plans against the active attached browser, optionally recording an unsurf trace

This is the “browser is the auth” path: the tool does not mint credentials or create a new browser profile; it uses the session you already authenticated.

Any client that supports the Streamable HTTP transport can connect. Point it at the `/mcp` endpoint and send standard JSON-RPC messages:

The server supports the `initialize`, `tools/list`, and `tools/call` methods.

You can verify the MCP endpoint works with plain `curl`.

You should get back a response with `serverInfo` and `capabilities`.

The response lists the registered tools. The hosted server includes `scout`, `worker`, `heal`, `gallery`, `unsurf_search`, and `unsurf_execute`; `directory` and `agent-scout` appear when their optional bindings are configured.

Beyond the scout/worker/heal set, the MCP server exposes two tools that work with the record/observe/loop skills — a pair-pattern (search + execute) so agents have a small, stable surface to reason over:

List recorded traces. Filter by owner, task substring, or visibility. Returns `viewerUrl` values with grants pre-minted, ready to open.

Run one of unsurf’s Worker-safe skills. Today:

- `loopPlan`- `LoopSpec`from a natural-language goal via Kimi K2.6. Plan only; no browser drive. Feed the result to the local- `unsurf loop`CLI (or- `loop()`JS API) to actually record.

Actions that need local Node APIs (actual `record()` via agent-browser, `observeVideo()` via ffmpeg) are CLI-only until the cloud recording provider lands (Phase 4 in [NORTHSTAR.md](https://github.com/acoyfellow/unsurf/blob/main/docs/NORTHSTAR.md)).

When you deploy your own unsurf instance, the MCP endpoint is automatically available at `/mcp` on your worker URL.

-
Clone the repo and install dependencies:
-
Set the required environment variables (see [Configuration](https://unsurf.coey.dev/reference/config#environment-variables)):
-
Deploy:
-
Point your MCP clients at your worker URL:

# How unsurf works | unsurf

Source: https://unsurf.coey.dev/concepts/how-it-works/

# How unsurf works

Agents often need to use websites that are already authenticated in a real browser. Fresh headless containers do not inherit that state, and copied credentials create a new security problem.

Unsurf starts from a different premise:

The local runtime attaches to an already-open Chrome/CDP session. Nearby agents can discover it through `unsurf-local-mcp`, or application code can use `recordAttachedLocal(...)` directly.

Recording wraps a browser run and produces:

- video
- action trace
- result metadata
- viewer links with grant-gated access

`observeVideo()` inspects those recordings. `loop()` composes record + observe + refine until a yes/no North Star is met.

When a website reveals a stable API beneath the UI, Unsurf can capture it:

- `scout`observes traffic and stores a typed seam
- `worker`replays it directly over HTTP
- `heal`repairs it when the site drifts

That path still matters. It is now one layer in a broader browser-runtime product, not the entire pitch.

| Surface | Best for |
|---|---|
| cmux browser | Canonical local authenticated investigation, snapshots, screenshots, and human takeover |
| Local browser MCP | Driving an attached Chrome/CDP session when that adapter is needed |
| Browser Run provider | Hosted isolated Cloudflare Worker-side BrowserHandle flows and native replay |
| `record`/`loop` | Producing inspectable proof from video-capable browser work |
| Hosted MCP / REST | Scouting, search, planning, and shared hosted surfaces |
| API replay | Repeated work that can skip the browser after discovery |

Hosted Unsurf runs on Cloudflare:

- Workers
- Workers AI
- Browser Rendering for hosted scouting
- D1 + R2 for stored specs, runs, and trace bundles

Browser providers are swappable behind Unsurf’s browser abstraction. The canonical local investigation provider is now cmux’s in-app browser. The `agent-browser` adapter remains available for attached Chrome/CDP and playable local video; it is not required for the normal investigation workflow.

- real browser auth beats invented delegation layers
- video makes browser work reviewable
- loops turn visual evidence into a stop condition
- typed API seams reduce repeat browser work when the web app gives you one

---

# Tutorial: your first unsurf

The shortest path now uses **cmux’s in-app browser**. `agent-browser` is not required for investigation, screenshots, portable repros, or broken/fixed confirmation.

Open cmux, then run:

Expected capabilities:

Sign in through the cmux browser as you normally would. Unsurf uses the browser profile you already trust; it does not mint or copy credentials.

Give Unsurf a vague symptom plus broken and fixed targets:

Unsurf opens several explicit cmux browser surfaces, promotes only an observed candidate, and confirms it three times against each target.

`repro.json`—not model prose—is the confirmation contract. The same artifact can move between previews and providers.

A new cmux surface gets separate page/tab state, but surfaces currently share the Default WebKit browser profile.

That is ideal for parallel authenticated exploration. For confirmation requiring clean identities, normalize application state, use separately configured profiles when available, or use Browser Run’s isolated hosted sessions.

If the deliverable specifically needs a local MP4/WebM, use Unsurf’s video-capable attached-Chrome provider. That legacy path currently uses `agent-browser`:

Then attach and record:

See [Record a browser session](https://unsurf.coey.dev/guides/record/) for the complete video workflow. Browser Run is the hosted alternative and produces native rrweb session replay rather than MP4.

# MCP Tools | unsurf

Source: https://unsurf.coey.dev/reference/tools/

The hosted unsurf MCP server registers six  default tools plus up to two  conditional tools. The local stdio server adds two browser-runtime tools.

Tool Availability `scout`Always `worker`Always `heal`Always `gallery`Always `directory`Requires `VECTORS` + `AI` bindings `agent-scout`Requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`

The separate local stdio server, `unsurf-local-mcp`, adds two browser-session tools for nearby agents:

Tool Availability `unsurf_local_sessions`Local only `unsurf_local_execute`Local only

List attachable page tabs from the local Chrome/CDP runtime that `unsurf-local-mcp` can drive.

Field Type Required Description `cdpPort``number`DevTools port to inspect. Defaults to `9222`.

Field Type Description `connected``boolean`Whether the local browser endpoint responded `sessions``array`Attachable page targets with tab id, title, and URL

Execute a small browser action plan against the attached local Chrome runtime. Actions include `goto`, `click`, `fill`, `wait`, `waitFor`, `snapshot`, and `screenshot`. Set `record: true` plus `task` to route the run through unsurf’s recorder.

Field Type Required Description `cdpPort``number`DevTools port to inspect. Defaults to `9222`. `actions``array`✅ Ordered browser action plan `record``boolean`Record the run through unsurf `task``string`Required when `record=true` Trace/task label `visibility``"private" | "public"`Recording visibility grant policy

Explore a website and capture its API endpoints.

Field Type Required Description `url``string`✅ Target URL to scout `task``string`✅ Natural language description of what to find `publish``boolean`Auto-publish the scouted site to the directory after scouting `auth``object`Authentication config `auth.cookies``string`Cookie header value `auth.headers``Record<string, string>`Additional request headers

Field Type Description `siteId``string`Unique identifier for the scouted site `endpointCount``number`Number of unique endpoints captured `pathId``string`Replayable navigation path ID `openApiSpec``object`OpenAPI 3.1 specification

# How to scout a website | unsurf

Source: https://unsurf.coey.dev/guides/scout/

# How to scout a website

`scout` is Unsurf’s seam-discovery path. Use it after, or instead of, browser work when the website exposes an underlying API worth reusing.

A good `task` names the interaction or seam you want, not just “explore the site.”

| Good | Weak |
|---|---|
| ”find the contact-form submit endpoint" | "find APIs" |
| "capture the dashboard data loader" | "explore the dashboard" |
| "map product search requests" | "test the store” |

The response includes:

- `siteId`
- `endpointCount`
- `pathId`
- `openApiSpec`

Use `pathId` with `worker`. Use the OpenAPI spec when you want a portable description of the discovered seam.

Use the browser runtime when the user’s authenticated session is the thing. Use scout when:

- the page exposes a stable API you want to call repeatedly
- direct HTTP replay will be cheaper or simpler than repeated UI work
- you want typed interface material for another integration

Hosted scout supports explicit cookies or headers, but for user-session work the preferred product path is still the local authenticated browser runtime. Scout is for seam discovery; local MCP is for operating the browser the user already trusts.

Set `publish: true` when the discovered seam belongs in the shared Directory. Otherwise keep the result private to your deploy.

---

# How to replay a captured API | unsurf

Source: https://unsurf.coey.dev/guides/replay/

# How to replay a captured API

After `scout` discovers a reusable seam, `worker` replays it directly over HTTP.

Choose worker when:

- you already know the seam
- the browser does not add value for this repeat operation
- you want millisecond-scale direct calls instead of a fresh UI walk

Choose the browser runtime when:

- the user session itself matters
- the action is visual or interaction-heavy
- you want a reviewable recorded proof

Worker can receive explicit request headers:

That is useful for programmatic integrations. It is not a replacement for the local “browser is the auth” path when you are acting inside the user’s existing live session.

If the API moved or response shape changed, call [heal](https://unsurf.coey.dev/guides/heal/).

---

# How to heal a broken seam | unsurf

Source: https://unsurf.coey.dev/guides/heal/

# How to heal a broken seam

`heal` belongs to Unsurf’s reusable-seam path. It is what keeps `worker` useful after a website changes.

- retries the original replay path,
- marks it broken if the failure persists,
- scouts the original site/task again,
- verifies the replacement,
- returns the new path.

| Situation | Use |
|---|---|
| A direct replay path drifted | `heal` |
| The browser task itself changed visually | update the browser plan or loop spec |
| The user-session task is still browser-native | stay on local browser MCP |

---

# Read a recorded browser session | unsurf

Source: https://unsurf.coey.dev/guides/observe/

# Read a recorded browser session

`observeVideo` is how Unsurf turns browser footage into a signal an agent can act on.

It returns:

- `answer`
- `confidence`
- `evidenceFrames`

Use `observeVideo` when:

- you recorded a browser run and need a compact answer
- another agent needs to inspect what happened without reading raw footage
- a loop needs a machine-readable success signal

- `ffmpeg`+- `ffprobe`
- Workers AI credentials for the default backends

Prefer bounded questions:

| Better | Worse |
|---|---|
| ”Did the page land on the authenticated dashboard?" | "What happened?" |
| "Was the submit button clicked?" | "Summarize everything." |
| "Did an error banner appear?" | "Was it good?” |

---

# Loop until the North Star | unsurf

Source: https://unsurf.coey.dev/guides/loop/

# Loop until the North Star

`loop()` composes the runtime:

Or attach to an already-open browser:

Good North Stars are:

- yes/no
- visible in the recording
- specific enough to stop on

Examples:

- “Did the authenticated dashboard load?”
- “Did the page reach a project detail view?”
- “Did all three form fields contain non-empty values?”

| Reason | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `met` | The recording satisfied the North Star |
| `abort` | Refiner gave up |
| `maxIterations` | Budget exhausted |
| `errorBudget` | Too many consecutive failures |

Use loop for browser-native work with a visual success condition. Use `worker` when a stable API seam has already been discovered and direct HTTP replay is the better interface.

---

# Private by default | unsurf

Source: https://unsurf.coey.dev/guides/privacy/

# Private by default

Browser recordings can contain sensitive UI state. Unsurf treats that as the default, not an edge case.

New traces return a signed `viewerUrl`. Bare `/r/<id>` URLs 404 for current uploads.

The viewer grant authorizes the trace page and related metadata for a limited window.

`public` still means grant-gated; it simply gets a longer-lived share link.

Revocation bumps the grant generation and invalidates previous links.

Unsurf is built around proof artifacts. Proof should be easy to share intentionally and hard to leak accidentally.

---

# How to use unsurf from an AI agent | unsurf

Source: https://unsurf.coey.dev/guides/agent-integration/

# How to use unsurf from an AI agent

Unsurf gives agents two complementary control planes:

- **local browser MCP**for the real authenticated browser on the user’s machine
- **hosted MCP**for shared scout/search/plan surfaces

Use:

- `unsurf_local_sessions`
- `unsurf_local_execute`

This is the right path for dashboards, apps behind login, and any task where the active user session matters.

Use hosted MCP for:

- `scout`
- `worker`
- `heal`
- trace search / planning surfaces

---

# Configuration | unsurf

Source: https://unsurf.coey.dev/reference/config/

# Configuration

For `unsurf investigate` and `unsurf replay`, open cmux and verify its in-app browser:

No `agent-browser` installation or CDP port is required. cmux provides authenticated interaction, snapshots, screenshots, and human takeover. Its Default WebKit profile is shared across surfaces, and WKWebView currently does not provide screencast, CDP trace, or network capture.

Install `agent-browser` only when you need playable local recording or an attached Chrome/CDP session:

The local MCP server defaults to CDP port `9222`; tool callers can pass a different `cdpPort` when needed.

unsurf uses [Alchemy](https://alchemy.run) to define hosted infrastructure as TypeScript. No YAML. No TOML.

```
import alchemy, { type StateStoreType } from "alchemy";
import type { Binding } from "alchemy/cloudflare";
import {
	Ai,
	BrowserRendering,
	CustomDomain,
	D1Database,
	KVNamespace,
	R2Bucket,
	RateLimit,
	VectorizeIndex,
	Worker,
} from "alchemy/cloudflare";
import { CloudflareStateStore } from "alchemy/state";
const stateStore: StateStoreType | undefined = process.env.ALCHEMY_STATE_TOKEN
	? (scope) => new CloudflareStateStore(scope)
	: undefined;
const app = await alchemy("unsurf", {
	password: process.env.ALCHEMY_PASSWORD || "dev-password",
	stage: process.env.ALCHEMY_STAGE || "production",
	...(stateStore ? { stateStore } : {}),
});
const DB = await D1Database("unsurf-db", {
	migrationsDir: "./migrations",
	adopt: true,
});
// Bundles are write-once, read-for-a-while. 90-day TTL keeps costs bounded
// and matches the retention we promise in docs. `trace/` prefix isolates
// the skill's objects from anything else the main worker writes.
const STORAGE = await R2Bucket("unsurf-storage", {
	adopt: true,
	lifecycle: [
		{
			id: "trace-bundles-90d",
			conditions: { prefix: "trace/" },
			enabled: true,
			deleteObjectsTransition: {
				condition: { type: "Age", maxAge: 90 * 24 * 60 * 60 },
			},
			storageClassTransitions: [
				{
					condition: { type: "Age", maxAge: 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 },
					storageClass: "InfrequentAccess",
				},
			],
		},
	],
});
const BROWSER = BrowserRendering();
const CACHE = await KVNamespace("unsurf-gallery-cache", {
	adopt: true,
});
// Vectorize index for semantic search + capability classification
const VECTORS = await VectorizeIndex("unsurf-vectors", {
	dimensions: 768,
	metric: "cosine",
	adopt: true,
});
const AI = Ai();
const bindings: Record<string, Binding> = {
	DB,
	STORAGE,
	BROWSER,
	CACHE,
	VECTORS,
	AI,
};
// Optional: pass Anthropic API key for LLM-guided scout
if (process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) {
	bindings.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = alchemy.secret(process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY);
}
// Bindings used by the unsurf MCP server (src/mcp.ts) for the
// `unsurf_search` and `unsurf_execute` tool pair:
//   TRACE_INGEST_TOKEN   — auth against trace.coey.dev for /search
//   CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID / CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN — Workers AI for
//     kimi-k2.6 planner used by unsurf_execute loopPlan
// All three are optional; the tools self-report misconfiguration.
if (process.env.TRACE_INGEST_TOKEN) {
	bindings.TRACE_INGEST_TOKEN = alchemy.secret(process.env.TRACE_INGEST_TOKEN);
}
if (process.env.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID) {
	bindings.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID = process.env.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID;
}
if (process.env.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN) {
	bindings.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN = alchemy.secret(process.env.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN);
}
export const WORKER = await Worker("unsurf", {
	name: "unsurf",
	entrypoint: "./src/cf-worker.ts",
	bindings,
	compatibility: "node",
	url: true,
	adopt: true,
});
// Custom domain for the API worker
await CustomDomain("unsurf-api-domain", {
	name: "unsurf-api.coey.dev",
	workerName: WORKER.name,
	adopt: true,
});
// ==================== trace viewer + ingest ====================
//
// Serves trace.coey.dev/r/:id (viewer) and /upload (ingest) for the `record`
// skill. v0.0.1 uses one Worker for both; split when there's >1 upload client.
// Required env vars at deploy time:
//   TRACE_SIGNING_KEY   32-byte hex (generate: openssl rand -hex 32)
//   TRACE_INGEST_TOKEN  random bearer string (generate: openssl rand -hex 32)
const traceSigningKey = process.env.TRACE_SIGNING_KEY;
const traceIngestToken = process.env.TRACE_INGEST_TOKEN;
if (!traceSigningKey || !traceIngestToken) {
	console.warn(
		"[unsurf-trace] TRACE_SIGNING_KEY and/or TRACE_INGEST_TOKEN missing; " +
			"using dev defaults. Generate real values with `openssl rand -hex 32` " +
			"before production deploys.",
	);
}
// KV namespace keyed by SHA-256(token) for per-user ingest credentials.
// Value shape: { owner, scope, createdAt, revokedAt?, quotaPerDay? }.
// Legacy TRACE_INGEST_TOKEN still authenticates as a fallback to preserve
// existing callers during migration.
const TRACE_TOKENS = await KVNamespace("unsurf-trace-tokens", {
	adopt: true,
});
// 120 uploads/minute per token hash is 2/s sustained — generous for real
// use, low enough to cap damage if a token leaks. Namespace id 1001 is
// arbitrary; must be stable across deploys.
const TRACE_INGEST_RATE_LIMIT = RateLimit({
	namespace_id: 1001,
	simple: { limit: 120, period: 60 },
});
export const TRACE_WORKER = await Worker("unsurf-trace", {
	name: "unsurf-trace",
	entrypoint: "./src/trace-worker.ts",
	bindings: {
		STORAGE,
		TRACE_TOKENS,
		TRACE_INGEST_RATE_LIMIT,
		TRACE_SIGNING_KEY: alchemy.secret(
			traceSigningKey || "dev-signing-key-replace-before-real-use-00000000",
		),
		TRACE_INGEST_TOKEN: alchemy.secret(
			traceIngestToken || "dev-ingest-token-replace-before-real-use",
		),
	},
	compatibility: "node",
	url: true,
	adopt: true,
});
await CustomDomain("unsurf-trace-domain", {
	name: "trace.coey.dev",
	workerName: TRACE_WORKER.name,
	adopt: true,
});
await app.finalize();
```
| Variable | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ALCHEMY_PASSWORD` | ✅ | Encrypts Alchemy’s local state file. Set any strong passphrase; changing it invalidates existing state. |
| `ALCHEMY_STATE_TOKEN` | Cloudflare API token scoped to Alchemy’s remote state store ( `CloudflareStateStore`). When set, state is persisted remotely instead of on disk — required for CI deploys. | |
| `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` | ✅ | Cloudflare API token with Workers, D1, R2, and Browser Runpermissions. Used by Alchemy to provision resources. |
| `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` | ✅ | Your Cloudflare account ID. Found at the top of the Cloudflare dashboard. |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Anthropic API key. Passed as a secret binding to the worker for LLM-guided scouting. Without it, scout falls back to heuristic-only mode. | |
| `ALCHEMY_STAGE` | Deployment stage ( `production`by default). Set to a different value to deploy an isolated copy (e.g.`staging`,`dev`). |

Set these in a `.env` file at the project root or export them in your shell before running `bun run deploy`.

These are configured automatically by Alchemy:

| Binding | Type | Name | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DB` | D1 Database | `unsurf-db` | Stores sites, endpoints, paths, run history |
| `STORAGE` | R2 Bucket | `unsurf-storage` | Stores HAR logs, screenshots, traces |
| `BROWSER` | Browser Run | — | Hosted browser flows, scouting, screenshots, and native rrweb session recordings via `recordBrowserRunSession(...)` |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Secret | — | Passed through as an encrypted secret binding (only when the env var is set) |
| `CACHE` | KV Namespace | `unsurf-cache` | Gallery response caching. Optional — gallery works without it but responses are not cached. |
| `VECTORS` | Vectorize Index | `unsurf-vectors` | Semantic search index for the API directory. Required for `/d/`directory and`/search`routes. |
| `AI` | Workers AI | — | Generates embeddings for Vectorize. Required alongside `VECTORS`for directory and search. |

unsurf uses [Drizzle ORM](https://orm.drizzle.team) with Cloudflare D1 (SQLite). Migrations are applied automatically by Alchemy on deploy — no manual migration steps are needed.

```
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { index, integer, sqliteTable, text, uniqueIndex } from "drizzle-orm/sqlite-core";
export const sites = sqliteTable("sites", {
	id: text("id").primaryKey(),
	url: text("url").notNull(),
	domain: text("domain").notNull(),
	firstScoutedAt: text("first_scouted_at").notNull(),
	lastScoutedAt: text("last_scouted_at").notNull(),
});
export const endpoints = sqliteTable(
	"endpoints",
	{
		id: text("id").primaryKey(),
		siteId: text("site_id")
			.notNull()
			.references(() => sites.id),
		method: text("method").notNull(),
		pathPattern: text("path_pattern").notNull(),
		requestSchema: text("request_schema"),
		responseSchema: text("response_schema"),
		requestHeaders: text("request_headers"),
		responseHeaders: text("response_headers"),
		sampleCount: integer("sample_count").notNull().default(1),
		firstSeenAt: text("first_seen_at").notNull(),
		lastSeenAt: text("last_seen_at").notNull(),
	},
	(table) => [
		uniqueIndex("endpoints_site_method_path").on(table.siteId, table.method, table.pathPattern),
	],
);
export const paths = sqliteTable("paths", {
	id: text("id").primaryKey(),
	siteId: text("site_id")
		.notNull()
		.references(() => sites.id),
	task: text("task").notNull(),
	steps: text("steps").notNull().default("[]"),
	endpointIds: text("endpoint_ids").notNull().default("[]"),
	status: text("status").notNull().default("active"),
	createdAt: text("created_at").notNull(),
	lastUsedAt: text("last_used_at"),
	failCount: integer("fail_count").notNull().default(0),
	healCount: integer("heal_count").notNull().default(0),
});
export const runs = sqliteTable("runs", {
	id: text("id").primaryKey(),
	pathId: text("path_id").references(() => paths.id),
	tool: text("tool").notNull(),
	status: text("status").notNull(),
	input: text("input").notNull(),
	output: text("output"),
	error: text("error"),
	durationMs: integer("duration_ms"),
	harKey: text("har_key"),
	createdAt: text("created_at").notNull(),
});
export const gallery = sqliteTable(
	"gallery",
	{
		id: text("id").primaryKey(),
		domain: text("domain").notNull(),
		url: text("url").notNull(),
		task: text("task").notNull(),
		endpointCount: integer("endpoint_count").notNull(),
		endpointsSummary: text("endpoints_summary").notNull(),
		specKey: text("spec_key").notNull(),
		contributor: text("contributor").default("anonymous"),
		createdAt: text("created_at").notNull(),
		updatedAt: text("updated_at").notNull(),
		version: integer("version").notNull().default(1),
	},
	(table) => [index("idx_gallery_domain").on(table.domain)],
);
// Directory tables for fingerprint-first architecture
export const fingerprints = sqliteTable(
	"fingerprints",
	{
		id: text("id").primaryKey(),
		domain: text("domain").notNull().unique(),
		url: text("url").notNull(),
		endpointCount: integer("endpoint_count").notNull(),
		capabilities: text("capabilities").notNull(), // JSON array
		methods: text("methods").notNull(), // JSON object {"GET": 5, "POST": 3}
		auth: text("auth").notNull(), // none|bearer|cookie|api-key|oauth|basic|unknown
		confidence: integer("confidence").notNull(), // 0-100 stored as int
		specKey: text("spec_key").notNull(), // R2 key for full OpenAPI
		contributor: text("contributor").default("anonymous"),
		createdAt: text("created_at").notNull(),
		updatedAt: text("updated_at").notNull(),
		version: integer("version").notNull().default(1),
	},
	(table) => [index("idx_fingerprints_domain").on(table.domain)],
);
export const directoryEndpoints = sqliteTable(
	"directory_endpoints",
	{
		id: text("id").primaryKey(),
		fingerprintId: text("fingerprint_id")
			.notNull()
			.references(() => fingerprints.id),
		method: text("method").notNull(),
		path: text("path").notNull(),
		summary: text("summary").notNull(),
		capability: text("capability").notNull(), // auth|payments|content|crud|...
		requestSchema: text("request_schema"), // JSON Schema as string
		responseSchema: text("response_schema"), // JSON Schema as string
		auth: integer("auth").notNull(), // 0 or 1
		exampleRequest: text("example_request"), // JSON
		exampleResponse: text("example_response"), // JSON
		vectorId: text("vector_id"), // ID in Vectorize for semantic search
	},
	(table) => [
		index("idx_directory_endpoints_fingerprint").on(table.fingerprintId),
		index("idx_directory_endpoints_capability").on(table.capability),
		uniqueIndex("idx_directory_endpoints_unique").on(table.fingerprintId, table.method, table.path),
	],
);
// FTS5 virtual table for full-text search on gallery
export const galleryFts = sql`
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS gallery_fts USING fts5(
	domain,
	url,
	task,
	endpoints_summary,
	content='gallery',
	content_rowid='rowid'
);
`;
// Triggers to keep gallery_fts in sync with gallery
export const galleryFtsSyncTriggers = [
	sql`
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS gallery_ai AFTER INSERT ON gallery BEGIN
	INSERT INTO gallery_fts(rowid, domain, url, task, endpoints_summary)
	VALUES (NEW.rowid, NEW.domain, NEW.url, NEW.task, NEW.endpoints_summary);
END;
`,
	sql`
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS gallery_ad AFTER DELETE ON gallery BEGIN
	INSERT INTO gallery_fts(gallery_fts, rowid, domain, url, task, endpoints_summary)
	VALUES ('delete', OLD.rowid, OLD.domain, OLD.url, OLD.task, OLD.endpoints_summary);
END;
`,
	sql`
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS gallery_au AFTER UPDATE ON gallery BEGIN
	INSERT INTO gallery_fts(gallery_fts, rowid, domain, url, task, endpoints_summary)
	VALUES ('delete', OLD.rowid, OLD.domain, OLD.url, OLD.task, OLD.endpoints_summary);
	INSERT INTO gallery_fts(rowid, domain, url, task, endpoints_summary)
	VALUES (NEW.rowid, NEW.domain, NEW.url, NEW.task, NEW.endpoints_summary);
END;
`,
];
export type Site = typeof sites.$inferSelect;
export type NewSite = typeof sites.$inferInsert;
export type Endpoint = typeof endpoints.$inferSelect;
export type NewEndpoint = typeof endpoints.$inferInsert;
export type Path = typeof paths.$inferSelect;
export type NewPath = typeof paths.$inferInsert;
export type Run = typeof runs.$inferSelect;
export type NewRun = typeof runs.$inferInsert;
export type Gallery = typeof gallery.$inferSelect;
export type NewGallery = typeof gallery.$inferInsert;
export type FingerprintRow = typeof fingerprints.$inferSelect;
export type NewFingerprintRow = typeof fingerprints.$inferInsert;
export type DirectoryEndpointRow = typeof directoryEndpoints.$inferSelect;
export type NewDirectoryEndpointRow = typeof directoryEndpoints.$inferInsert;
```
One row per distinct website that has been scouted.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `text`PK | Unique site identifier (e.g. `site_lx1a_k9m3`) |
| `url` | `text` | The URL that was passed to `scout` |
| `domain` | `text` | Extracted hostname — used for grouping and deduplication |
| `first_scouted_at` | `text`(ISO 8601) | Timestamp of the first scout |
| `last_scouted_at` | `text`(ISO 8601) | Timestamp of the most recent scout |

Every unique API call observed during scouting. A site has many endpoints. Endpoints are deduplicated by the composite unique index `(site_id, method, path_pattern)`.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `text`PK | Unique endpoint identifier |
| `site_id` | `text`FK →`sites.id` | The site this endpoint belongs to |
| `method` | `text` | HTTP method ( `GET`,`POST`, etc.) |
| `path_pattern` | `text` | URL path with parameter placeholders (e.g. `/api/v1/users/:id`) |
| `request_schema` | `text`(JSON) | JSON Schema of the request body, inferred from observed traffic |
| `response_schema` | `text`(JSON) | JSON Schema of the response body |
| `request_headers` | `text`(JSON) | Notable request headers (auth tokens, content types) |
| `response_headers` | `text`(JSON) | Notable response headers |
| `sample_count` | `integer` | How many times this endpoint was observed (higher = more confident schema) |
| `first_seen_at` | `text`(ISO 8601) | When this endpoint was first captured |
| `last_seen_at` | `text`(ISO 8601) | When this endpoint was last captured |

A replayable sequence of steps that accomplishes a task on a site. Created by `scout`, executed by `worker`, repaired by `heal`. A site can have many paths; each path references one or more endpoints.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `text`PK | Unique path identifier (returned as `pathId`) |
| `site_id` | `text`FK →`sites.id` | The site this path belongs to |
| `task` | `text` | The natural-language task passed to `scout` |
| `steps` | `text`(JSON array) | Ordered list of HTTP calls to replay |
| `endpoint_ids` | `text`(JSON array) | IDs of the endpoints this path touches |
| `status` | `text` | `active`,`broken`, or`healing` |
| `created_at` | `text`(ISO 8601) | When the path was created |
| `last_used_at` | `text`(ISO 8601) | When `worker`last executed this path |
| `fail_count` | `integer` | Consecutive failures (reset to 0 on success) |
| `heal_count` | `integer` | Total number of successful heals |

Audit log of every tool invocation — scout, worker, and heal. Used for debugging, monitoring, and billing.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `text`PK | Unique run identifier |
| `path_id` | `text`FK →`paths.id` | The path this run relates to (null for scout runs on new sites) |
| `tool` | `text` | Which tool ran: `scout`,`worker`, or`heal` |
| `status` | `text` | `success`or`failure` |
| `input` | `text`(JSON) | The full input passed to the tool |
| `output` | `text`(JSON) | The tool’s result (null on failure) |
| `error` | `text` | Error message (null on success) |
| `duration_ms` | `integer` | Wall-clock time of the run |
| `har_key` | `text` | R2 object key for the HAR recording (scout runs only) |
| `created_at` | `text`(ISO 8601) | When the run started |

- A **site**has many**endpoints**(all API calls observed) and many**paths**(replayable task sequences).
- A **path**belongs to one site and references specific endpoints via`endpoint_ids`.
- A **run**belongs to one path and records a single tool invocation.

The worker exposes a JSON REST API alongside the MCP endpoint.

Health check and service metadata.

**Response** `200`

Explore a website and capture its API endpoints.

**Request body**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | `string` | ✅ | Target URL to scout |
| `task` | `string` | ✅ | Natural-language description of what to find |

**Response** `200`

**Errors**

| Status | Body | When |
|---|---|---|
| `400` | `{"error": "Missing 'url' and 'task' in request body"}` | Required fields missing |
| `500` | `{"error": "..."}` | Browser, network, or storage failure |

Replay a scouted path — executes the captured API calls directly, no browser needed.

**Request body**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pathId` | `string` | ✅ | Path ID from a previous scout |
| `data` | `object` | Data to interpolate into the request |

**Response** `200`

**Errors**

| Status | Body | When |
|---|---|---|
| `400` | `{"error": "Missing 'pathId' in request body"}` | Required field missing |
| `500` | `{"error": "PathBrokenError: POST /api/v1/users returned 404"}` | Path is broken — call heal |
| `500` | `{"error": "..."}` | Network or storage failure |

Repair a broken path by retrying, then re-scouting if retries fail.

**Request body**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pathId` | `string` | ✅ | ID of the broken path |
| `error` | `string` | Description of what went wrong — helps the re-scout |

**Response** `200`

**Errors**

| Status | Body | When |
|---|---|---|
| `400` | `{"error": "Missing 'pathId' in request body"}` | Required field missing |
| `500` | `{"error": "..."}` | Browser, network, or storage failure |

MCP (Streamable HTTP) endpoint. See [MCP Server guide](https://unsurf.coey.dev/guides/mcp) and [MCP Tools reference](https://unsurf.coey.dev/reference/tools).

All endpoints return permissive CORS headers (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`). `OPTIONS` preflight requests are handled automatically.

Any other method/path combination returns `404`:

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `bun run dev` | Local development via Alchemy |
| `bun run deploy` | Deploy to Cloudflare |
| `bun run generate` | Generate Drizzle migrations (internal dev workflow — not needed for deployment) |
| `bun run test` | Run test suite |
| `bun run check` | Lint and format (Biome) |
| `bun run typecheck` | TypeScript type checking |

# Agent interaction patterns | unsurf

Source: https://unsurf.coey.dev/concepts/agent-patterns/

# Agent interaction patterns

| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| Operate the browser the user already authenticated | `unsurf-local-mcp` |
| Record a browser run for review | `record`/`recordAttachedLocal` |
| Retry until visual success is proven | `loop` |
| Ask what happened in a run | `observeVideo` |
| Reuse a stable hidden HTTP seam | `scout`→`worker`→`heal` |

Use local MCP when another nearby agent should act inside the user’s real session:

Typical flow:

- call `unsurf_local_sessions`
- inspect the attachable tabs
- call `unsurf_local_execute`
- optionally record the action plan

This is the right path for authenticated dashboards, enterprise apps, and any work where the browser identity matters.

If the task matters enough to review later, record it:

A proof bundle gives the agent and the human a shared artifact: the browser video, trace, status, and viewer link.

## Pattern 3 — Loop until the North Star is met

[Section titled “Pattern 3 — Loop until the North Star is met”](https://unsurf.coey.dev#pattern-3--loop-until-the-north-star-is-met)

Use `loop()` when the success condition is visual or interaction-heavy:

Good North Stars are yes/no and observable from the recording.

If an operation repeats often and the browser exposes a stable HTTP endpoint, use:

That path is still excellent for search APIs, data loaders, and repeatable CRUD-like flows. It is simply not the only Unsurf workflow.

| Failure | Agent response |
|---|---|
| No local browser sessions | Ask the user to open/authenticate the browser runtime |
| Browser action fails | Stop the plan, return the failing action, do not blindly continue |
| Loop misses North Star | Refine or stop at budget |
| `worker`path drifts | Call `heal` |

---

# MCP Tools | unsurf

Source: https://unsurf.coey.dev/reference/tools

The hosted unsurf MCP server registers six  default tools plus up to two  conditional tools. The local stdio server adds two browser-runtime tools.

Tool Availability `scout`Always `worker`Always `heal`Always `gallery`Always `directory`Requires `VECTORS` + `AI` bindings `agent-scout`Requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`

The separate local stdio server, `unsurf-local-mcp`, adds two browser-session tools for nearby agents:

Tool Availability `unsurf_local_sessions`Local only `unsurf_local_execute`Local only

List attachable page tabs from the local Chrome/CDP runtime that `unsurf-local-mcp` can drive.

Field Type Required Description `cdpPort``number`DevTools port to inspect. Defaults to `9222`.

Field Type Description `connected``boolean`Whether the local browser endpoint responded `sessions``array`Attachable page targets with tab id, title, and URL

Execute a small browser action plan against the attached local Chrome runtime. Actions include `goto`, `click`, `fill`, `wait`, `waitFor`, `snapshot`, and `screenshot`. Set `record: true` plus `task` to route the run through unsurf’s recorder.

Field Type Required Description `cdpPort``number`DevTools port to inspect. Defaults to `9222`. `actions``array`✅ Ordered browser action plan `record``boolean`Record the run through unsurf `task``string`Required when `record=true` Trace/task label `visibility``"private" | "public"`Recording visibility grant policy

Explore a website and capture its API endpoints.

Field Type Required Description `url``string`✅ Target URL to scout `task``string`✅ Natural language description of what to find `publish``boolean`Auto-publish the scouted site to the directory after scouting `auth``object`Authentication config `auth.cookies``string`Cookie header value `auth.headers``Record<string, string>`Additional request headers

Field Type Description `siteId``string`Unique identifier for the scouted site `endpointCount``number`Number of unique endpoints captured `pathId``string`Replayable navigation path ID `openApiSpec``object`OpenAPI 3.1 specification

Error When `BrowserError`Browser container failed to launch or crashed `NetworkError`Target site unreachable `StoreError`Failed to save results to D1/R2

   "description" :  " Explore a website and capture every API call. Returns captured endpoints with inferred schemas and an OpenAPI spec. " ,

     "required" : [ " url " ,  " task " ],

       "url" : {  "type" :  " string " ,  "description" :  " The URL to scout "  },

       "task" : {  "type" :  " string " ,  "description" :  " What to look for, e.g. 'find all API endpoints' "  },

       "publish" : {  "type" :  " boolean " ,  "description" :  " Auto-publish the scouted site to the directory after scouting "  }

Execute a scouted path or replay a captured API endpoint.

Field Type Required Description `pathId``string`✅ ID of the path to execute `data``Record<string, unknown>`Data to pass to the endpoint `headers``Record<string, string>`Custom headers (`Authorization`, `Cookie`, etc.) for authenticated endpoints

Field Type Description `success``boolean`Whether execution succeeded `response``unknown`Response body from the target API

Error When `NotFoundError`Path ID does not exist `PathBrokenError`Path is broken — target site changed `NetworkError`Target API unreachable `BrowserError`Browser fallback failed

   "description" :  " Replay a scouted API path directly — no browser needed. Pass the pathId from a scout result. Include headers for authenticated endpoints. " ,

       "pathId" : {  "type" :  " string " ,  "description" :  " The path ID from a scout result "  },

       "data" : {  "type" :  " object " ,  "description" :  " Data to pass to the endpoint "  },

       "headers" : {  "type" :  " object " ,  "description" :  " Custom headers (Authorization, Cookie, etc.) for authenticated endpoints "  }

Re-scout and repair a broken path.

Field Type Required Description `pathId``string`✅ ID of the broken path `error``string`Description of what went wrong

Field Type Description `healed``boolean`Whether the path was successfully repaired `newPathId``string`ID of the new path (if changed)

Error When `NotFoundError`Path ID does not exist `BrowserError`Re-scout browser failed `NetworkError`Target site unreachable

   "description" :  " Fix a broken path. Retries with backoff, then re-scouts and patches if needed. " ,

       "pathId" : {  "type" :  " string " ,  "description" :  " The broken path ID "  },

       "error" : {  "type" :  " string " ,  "description" :  " The error message that caused the break "  }

Search the API gallery for previously unsurfed sites. Check here before scouting — someone may have already captured the API you need.

Field Type Required Description `query``string`Search term (domain, endpoint path, or description) `domain``string`Exact domain to look up

Field Type Description `results``array`Matching gallery entries `total``number`Number of results returned

   "description" :  " Search the API gallery for previously unsurfed sites. Check here before scouting — someone may have already captured the API you need. " ,

       "query" : {  "type" :  " string " ,  "description" :  " Search term (domain, endpoint path, or description) "  },

       "domain" : {  "type" :  " string " ,  "description" :  " Exact domain to look up "  }

Fingerprint-first API directory. Look up domains, browse capabilities, inspect endpoints, semantic search, or publish scouted sites. Returns token-efficient fingerprints, not full specs.

Field Type Required Description `action``"fingerprint" | "capability" | "endpoint" | "search" | "publish"`✅ The directory action to perform `domain``string`Domain to look up (required for `fingerprint`, `capability`, `endpoint`) `capability``string`Capability category (required for `capability` action). One of: `auth`, `payments`, `content`, `crud`, `search`, `messaging`, `files`, `analytics`, `social`, `ecommerce`, `forms`, `other` `method``string`HTTP method (required for `endpoint` action) `path``string`Endpoint path (required for `endpoint` action) `query``string`Search query (required for `search` action) `siteId``string`Site ID from a scout result (required for `publish` action)

Action Required fields Description Token cost `fingerprint``domain`Get domain overview ~50 tokens `capability``domain`, `capability`List endpoints by capability ~200 tokens `endpoint``domain`, `method`, `path`Single endpoint detail ~80 tokens `search``query`Semantic search across all APIs varies `publish``siteId`Add a scouted site to the directory varies

   "description" :  " Fingerprint-first API directory. Look up domains, browse capabilities, inspect endpoints, semantic search, or publish scouted sites. " ,

       "action" : {  "type" :  " string " ,  "enum" : [ " fingerprint " ,  " capability " ,  " endpoint " ,  " search " ,  " publish " ] },

       "domain" : {  "type" :  " string " ,  "description" :  " Domain to look up "  },

       "capability" : {  "type" :  " string " ,  "enum" : [ " auth " ,  " payments " ,  " content " ,  " crud " ,  " search " ,  " messaging " ,  " files " ,  " analytics " ,  " social " ,  " ecommerce " ,  " forms " ,  " other " ] },

       "method" : {  "type" :  " string " ,  "description" :  " HTTP method "  },

       "path" : {  "type" :  " string " ,  "description" :  " Endpoint path "  },

       "query" : {  "type" :  " string " ,  "description" :  " Search query "  },

       "siteId" : {  "type" :  " string " ,  "description" :  " Site ID from a scout result "  }

LLM-guided exploration — an AI agent clicks, types, and navigates to find more API endpoints than a simple page load.

Field Type Required Description `url``string`✅ The URL to explore `task``string`✅ What to look for and do on the site

Field Type Description `steps``array`Sequence of actions the agent took `networkEventsCount``number`Total network events captured `events``array`Captured network events (`method`, `url`, `status`)

   "description" :  " LLM-guided exploration — an AI agent clicks, types, and navigates to find more API endpoints than a simple page load. " ,

     "required" : [ " url " ,  " task " ],

       "url" : {  "type" :  " string " ,  "description" :  " The URL to explore "  },

       "task" : {  "type" :  " string " ,  "description" :  " What to look for and do on the site "  }

---

# Configuration | unsurf

Source: https://unsurf.coey.dev/reference/config

# Configuration

For `unsurf investigate` and `unsurf replay`, open cmux and verify its in-app browser:

No `agent-browser` installation or CDP port is required. cmux provides authenticated interaction, snapshots, screenshots, and human takeover. Its Default WebKit profile is shared across surfaces, and WKWebView currently does not provide screencast, CDP trace, or network capture.

Install `agent-browser` only when you need playable local recording or an attached Chrome/CDP session:

The local MCP server defaults to CDP port `9222`; tool callers can pass a different `cdpPort` when needed.

unsurf uses [Alchemy](https://alchemy.run) to define hosted infrastructure as TypeScript. No YAML. No TOML.

```
import alchemy, { type StateStoreType } from "alchemy";
import type { Binding } from "alchemy/cloudflare";
import {
	Ai,
	BrowserRendering,
	CustomDomain,
	D1Database,
	KVNamespace,
	R2Bucket,
	RateLimit,
	VectorizeIndex,
	Worker,
} from "alchemy/cloudflare";
import { CloudflareStateStore } from "alchemy/state";
const stateStore: StateStoreType | undefined = process.env.ALCHEMY_STATE_TOKEN
	? (scope) => new CloudflareStateStore(scope)
	: undefined;
const app = await alchemy("unsurf", {
	password: process.env.ALCHEMY_PASSWORD || "dev-password",
	stage: process.env.ALCHEMY_STAGE || "production",
	...(stateStore ? { stateStore } : {}),
});
const DB = await D1Database("unsurf-db", {
	migrationsDir: "./migrations",
	adopt: true,
});
// Bundles are write-once, read-for-a-while. 90-day TTL keeps costs bounded
// and matches the retention we promise in docs. `trace/` prefix isolates
// the skill's objects from anything else the main worker writes.
const STORAGE = await R2Bucket("unsurf-storage", {
	adopt: true,
	lifecycle: [
		{
			id: "trace-bundles-90d",
			conditions: { prefix: "trace/" },
			enabled: true,
			deleteObjectsTransition: {
				condition: { type: "Age", maxAge: 90 * 24 * 60 * 60 },
			},
			storageClassTransitions: [
				{
					condition: { type: "Age", maxAge: 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 },
					storageClass: "InfrequentAccess",
				},
			],
		},
	],
});
const BROWSER = BrowserRendering();
const CACHE = await KVNamespace("unsurf-gallery-cache", {
	adopt: true,
});
// Vectorize index for semantic search + capability classification
const VECTORS = await VectorizeIndex("unsurf-vectors", {
	dimensions: 768,
	metric: "cosine",
	adopt: true,
});
const AI = Ai();
const bindings: Record<string, Binding> = {
	DB,
	STORAGE,
	BROWSER,
	CACHE,
	VECTORS,
	AI,
};
// Optional: pass Anthropic API key for LLM-guided scout
if (process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) {
	bindings.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = alchemy.secret(process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY);
}
// Bindings used by the unsurf MCP server (src/mcp.ts) for the
// `unsurf_search` and `unsurf_execute` tool pair:
//   TRACE_INGEST_TOKEN   — auth against trace.coey.dev for /search
//   CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID / CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN — Workers AI for
//     kimi-k2.6 planner used by unsurf_execute loopPlan
// All three are optional; the tools self-report misconfiguration.
if (process.env.TRACE_INGEST_TOKEN) {
	bindings.TRACE_INGEST_TOKEN = alchemy.secret(process.env.TRACE_INGEST_TOKEN);
}
if (process.env.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID) {
	bindings.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID = process.env.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID;
}
if (process.env.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN) {
	bindings.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN = alchemy.secret(process.env.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN);
}
export const WORKER = await Worker("unsurf", {
	name: "unsurf",
	entrypoint: "./src/cf-worker.ts",
	bindings,
	compatibility: "node",
	url: true,
	adopt: true,
});
// Custom domain for the API worker
await CustomDomain("unsurf-api-domain", {
	name: "unsurf-api.coey.dev",
	workerName: WORKER.name,
	adopt: true,
});
// ==================== trace viewer + ingest ====================
//
// Serves trace.coey.dev/r/:id (viewer) and /upload (ingest) for the `record`
// skill. v0.0.1 uses one Worker for both; split when there's >1 upload client.
// Required env vars at deploy time:
//   TRACE_SIGNING_KEY   32-byte hex (generate: openssl rand -hex 32)
//   TRACE_INGEST_TOKEN  random bearer string (generate: openssl rand -hex 32)
const traceSigningKey = process.env.TRACE_SIGNING_KEY;
const traceIngestToken = process.env.TRACE_INGEST_TOKEN;
if (!traceSigningKey || !traceIngestToken) {
	console.warn(
		"[unsurf-trace] TRACE_SIGNING_KEY and/or TRACE_INGEST_TOKEN missing; " +
			"using dev defaults. Generate real values with `openssl rand -hex 32` " +
			"before production deploys.",
	);
}
// KV namespace keyed by SHA-256(token) for per-user ingest credentials.
// Value shape: { owner, scope, createdAt, revokedAt?, quotaPerDay? }.
// Legacy TRACE_INGEST_TOKEN still authenticates as a fallback to preserve
// existing callers during migration.
const TRACE_TOKENS = await KVNamespace("unsurf-trace-tokens", {
	adopt: true,
});
// 120 uploads/minute per token hash is 2/s sustained — generous for real
// use, low enough to cap damage if a token leaks. Namespace id 1001 is
// arbitrary; must be stable across deploys.
const TRACE_INGEST_RATE_LIMIT = RateLimit({
	namespace_id: 1001,
	simple: { limit: 120, period: 60 },
});
export const TRACE_WORKER = await Worker("unsurf-trace", {
	name: "unsurf-trace",
	entrypoint: "./src/trace-worker.ts",
	bindings: {
		STORAGE,
		TRACE_TOKENS,
		TRACE_INGEST_RATE_LIMIT,
		TRACE_SIGNING_KEY: alchemy.secret(
			traceSigningKey || "dev-signing-key-replace-before-real-use-00000000",
		),
		TRACE_INGEST_TOKEN: alchemy.secret(
			traceIngestToken || "dev-ingest-token-replace-before-real-use",
		),
	},
	compatibility: "node",
	url: true,
	adopt: true,
});
await CustomDomain("unsurf-trace-domain", {
	name: "trace.coey.dev",
	workerName: TRACE_WORKER.name,
	adopt: true,
});
await app.finalize();
```
| Variable | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ALCHEMY_PASSWORD` | ✅ | Encrypts Alchemy’s local state file. Set any strong passphrase; changing it invalidates existing state. |
| `ALCHEMY_STATE_TOKEN` | Cloudflare API token scoped to Alchemy’s remote state store ( `CloudflareStateStore`). When set, state is persisted remotely instead of on disk — required for CI deploys. | |
| `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` | ✅ | Cloudflare API token with Workers, D1, R2, and Browser Runpermissions. Used by Alchemy to provision resources. |
| `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` | ✅ | Your Cloudflare account ID. Found at the top of the Cloudflare dashboard. |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Anthropic API key. Passed as a secret binding to the worker for LLM-guided scouting. Without it, scout falls back to heuristic-only mode. | |
| `ALCHEMY_STAGE` | Deployment stage ( `production`by default). Set to a different value to deploy an isolated copy (e.g.`staging`,`dev`). |

Set these in a `.env` file at the project root or export them in your shell before running `bun run deploy`.

These are configured automatically by Alchemy:

| Binding | Type | Name | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DB` | D1 Database | `unsurf-db` | Stores sites, endpoints, paths, run history |
| `STORAGE` | R2 Bucket | `unsurf-storage` | Stores HAR logs, screenshots, traces |
| `BROWSER` | Browser Run | — | Hosted browser flows, scouting, screenshots, and native rrweb session recordings via `recordBrowserRunSession(...)` |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Secret | — | Passed through as an encrypted secret binding (only when the env var is set) |
| `CACHE` | KV Namespace | `unsurf-cache` | Gallery response caching. Optional — gallery works without it but responses are not cached. |
| `VECTORS` | Vectorize Index | `unsurf-vectors` | Semantic search index for the API directory. Required for `/d/`directory and`/search`routes. |
| `AI` | Workers AI | — | Generates embeddings for Vectorize. Required alongside `VECTORS`for directory and search. |

unsurf uses [Drizzle ORM](https://orm.drizzle.team) with Cloudflare D1 (SQLite). Migrations are applied automatically by Alchemy on deploy — no manual migration steps are needed.

```
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { index, integer, sqliteTable, text, uniqueIndex } from "drizzle-orm/sqlite-core";
export const sites = sqliteTable("sites", {
	id: text("id").primaryKey(),
	url: text("url").notNull(),
	domain: text("domain").notNull(),
	firstScoutedAt: text("first_scouted_at").notNull(),
	lastScoutedAt: text("last_scouted_at").notNull(),
});
export const endpoints = sqliteTable(
	"endpoints",
	{
		id: text("id").primaryKey(),
		siteId: text("site_id")
			.notNull()
			.references(() => sites.id),
		method: text("method").notNull(),
		pathPattern: text("path_pattern").notNull(),
		requestSchema: text("request_schema"),
		responseSchema: text("response_schema"),
		requestHeaders: text("request_headers"),
		responseHeaders: text("response_headers"),
		sampleCount: integer("sample_count").notNull().default(1),
		firstSeenAt: text("first_seen_at").notNull(),
		lastSeenAt: text("last_seen_at").notNull(),
	},
	(table) => [
		uniqueIndex("endpoints_site_method_path").on(table.siteId, table.method, table.pathPattern),
	],
);
export const paths = sqliteTable("paths", {
	id: text("id").primaryKey(),
	siteId: text("site_id")
		.notNull()
		.references(() => sites.id),
	task: text("task").notNull(),
	steps: text("steps").notNull().default("[]"),
	endpointIds: text("endpoint_ids").notNull().default("[]"),
	status: text("status").notNull().default("active"),
	createdAt: text("created_at").notNull(),
	lastUsedAt: text("last_used_at"),
	failCount: integer("fail_count").notNull().default(0),
	healCount: integer("heal_count").notNull().default(0),
});
export const runs = sqliteTable("runs", {
	id: text("id").primaryKey(),
	pathId: text("path_id").references(() => paths.id),
	tool: text("tool").notNull(),
	status: text("status").notNull(),
	input: text("input").notNull(),
	output: text("output"),
	error: text("error"),
	durationMs: integer("duration_ms"),
	harKey: text("har_key"),
	createdAt: text("created_at").notNull(),
});
export const gallery = sqliteTable(
	"gallery",
	{
		id: text("id").primaryKey(),
		domain: text("domain").notNull(),
		url: text("url").notNull(),
		task: text("task").notNull(),
		endpointCount: integer("endpoint_count").notNull(),
		endpointsSummary: text("endpoints_summary").notNull(),
		specKey: text("spec_key").notNull(),
		contributor: text("contributor").default("anonymous"),
		createdAt: text("created_at").notNull(),
		updatedAt: text("updated_at").notNull(),
		version: integer("version").notNull().default(1),
	},
	(table) => [index("idx_gallery_domain").on(table.domain)],
);
// Directory tables for fingerprint-first architecture
export const fingerprints = sqliteTable(
	"fingerprints",
	{
		id: text("id").primaryKey(),
		domain: text("domain").notNull().unique(),
		url: text("url").notNull(),
		endpointCount: integer("endpoint_count").notNull(),
		capabilities: text("capabilities").notNull(), // JSON array
		methods: text("methods").notNull(), // JSON object {"GET": 5, "POST": 3}
		auth: text("auth").notNull(), // none|bearer|cookie|api-key|oauth|basic|unknown
		confidence: integer("confidence").notNull(), // 0-100 stored as int
		specKey: text("spec_key").notNull(), // R2 key for full OpenAPI
		contributor: text("contributor").default("anonymous"),
		createdAt: text("created_at").notNull(),
		updatedAt: text("updated_at").notNull(),
		version: integer("version").notNull().default(1),
	},
	(table) => [index("idx_fingerprints_domain").on(table.domain)],
);
export const directoryEndpoints = sqliteTable(
	"directory_endpoints",
	{
		id: text("id").primaryKey(),
		fingerprintId: text("fingerprint_id")
			.notNull()
			.references(() => fingerprints.id),
		method: text("method").notNull(),
		path: text("path").notNull(),
		summary: text("summary").notNull(),
		capability: text("capability").notNull(), // auth|payments|content|crud|...
		requestSchema: text("request_schema"), // JSON Schema as string
		responseSchema: text("response_schema"), // JSON Schema as string
		auth: integer("auth").notNull(), // 0 or 1
		exampleRequest: text("example_request"), // JSON
		exampleResponse: text("example_response"), // JSON
		vectorId: text("vector_id"), // ID in Vectorize for semantic search
	},
	(table) => [
		index("idx_directory_endpoints_fingerprint").on(table.fingerprintId),
		index("idx_directory_endpoints_capability").on(table.capability),
		uniqueIndex("idx_directory_endpoints_unique").on(table.fingerprintId, table.method, table.path),
	],
);
// FTS5 virtual table for full-text search on gallery
export const galleryFts = sql`
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS gallery_fts USING fts5(
	domain,
	url,
	task,
	endpoints_summary,
	content='gallery',
	content_rowid='rowid'
);
`;
// Triggers to keep gallery_fts in sync with gallery
export const galleryFtsSyncTriggers = [
	sql`
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS gallery_ai AFTER INSERT ON gallery BEGIN
	INSERT INTO gallery_fts(rowid, domain, url, task, endpoints_summary)
	VALUES (NEW.rowid, NEW.domain, NEW.url, NEW.task, NEW.endpoints_summary);
END;
`,
	sql`
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS gallery_ad AFTER DELETE ON gallery BEGIN
	INSERT INTO gallery_fts(gallery_fts, rowid, domain, url, task, endpoints_summary)
	VALUES ('delete', OLD.rowid, OLD.domain, OLD.url, OLD.task, OLD.endpoints_summary);
END;
`,
	sql`
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS gallery_au AFTER UPDATE ON gallery BEGIN
	INSERT INTO gallery_fts(gallery_fts, rowid, domain, url, task, endpoints_summary)
	VALUES ('delete', OLD.rowid, OLD.domain, OLD.url, OLD.task, OLD.endpoints_summary);
	INSERT INTO gallery_fts(rowid, domain, url, task, endpoints_summary)
	VALUES (NEW.rowid, NEW.domain, NEW.url, NEW.task, NEW.endpoints_summary);
END;
`,
];
export type Site = typeof sites.$inferSelect;
export type NewSite = typeof sites.$inferInsert;
export type Endpoint = typeof endpoints.$inferSelect;
export type NewEndpoint = typeof endpoints.$inferInsert;
export type Path = typeof paths.$inferSelect;
export type NewPath = typeof paths.$inferInsert;
export type Run = typeof runs.$inferSelect;
export type NewRun = typeof runs.$inferInsert;
export type Gallery = typeof gallery.$inferSelect;
export type NewGallery = typeof gallery.$inferInsert;
export type FingerprintRow = typeof fingerprints.$inferSelect;
export type NewFingerprintRow = typeof fingerprints.$inferInsert;
export type DirectoryEndpointRow = typeof directoryEndpoints.$inferSelect;
export type NewDirectoryEndpointRow = typeof directoryEndpoints.$inferInsert;
```
One row per distinct website that has been scouted.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `text`PK | Unique site identifier (e.g. `site_lx1a_k9m3`) |
| `url` | `text` | The URL that was passed to `scout` |
| `domain` | `text` | Extracted hostname — used for grouping and deduplication |
| `first_scouted_at` | `text`(ISO 8601) | Timestamp of the first scout |
| `last_scouted_at` | `text`(ISO 8601) | Timestamp of the most recent scout |

Every unique API call observed during scouting. A site has many endpoints. Endpoints are deduplicated by the composite unique index `(site_id, method, path_pattern)`.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `text`PK | Unique endpoint identifier |
| `site_id` | `text`FK →`sites.id` | The site this endpoint belongs to |
| `method` | `text` | HTTP method ( `GET`,`POST`, etc.) |
| `path_pattern` | `text` | URL path with parameter placeholders (e.g. `/api/v1/users/:id`) |
| `request_schema` | `text`(JSON) | JSON Schema of the request body, inferred from observed traffic |
| `response_schema` | `text`(JSON) | JSON Schema of the response body |
| `request_headers` | `text`(JSON) | Notable request headers (auth tokens, content types) |
| `response_headers` | `text`(JSON) | Notable response headers |
| `sample_count` | `integer` | How many times this endpoint was observed (higher = more confident schema) |
| `first_seen_at` | `text`(ISO 8601) | When this endpoint was first captured |
| `last_seen_at` | `text`(ISO 8601) | When this endpoint was last captured |

A replayable sequence of steps that accomplishes a task on a site. Created by `scout`, executed by `worker`, repaired by `heal`. A site can have many paths; each path references one or more endpoints.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `text`PK | Unique path identifier (returned as `pathId`) |
| `site_id` | `text`FK →`sites.id` | The site this path belongs to |
| `task` | `text` | The natural-language task passed to `scout` |
| `steps` | `text`(JSON array) | Ordered list of HTTP calls to replay |
| `endpoint_ids` | `text`(JSON array) | IDs of the endpoints this path touches |
| `status` | `text` | `active`,`broken`, or`healing` |
| `created_at` | `text`(ISO 8601) | When the path was created |
| `last_used_at` | `text`(ISO 8601) | When `worker`last executed this path |
| `fail_count` | `integer` | Consecutive failures (reset to 0 on success) |
| `heal_count` | `integer` | Total number of successful heals |

Audit log of every tool invocation — scout, worker, and heal. Used for debugging, monitoring, and billing.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `text`PK | Unique run identifier |
| `path_id` | `text`FK →`paths.id` | The path this run relates to (null for scout runs on new sites) |
| `tool` | `text` | Which tool ran: `scout`,`worker`, or`heal` |
| `status` | `text` | `success`or`failure` |
| `input` | `text`(JSON) | The full input passed to the tool |
| `output` | `text`(JSON) | The tool’s result (null on failure) |
| `error` | `text` | Error message (null on success) |
| `duration_ms` | `integer` | Wall-clock time of the run |
| `har_key` | `text` | R2 object key for the HAR recording (scout runs only) |
| `created_at` | `text`(ISO 8601) | When the run started |

- A **site**has many**endpoints**(all API calls observed) and many**paths**(replayable task sequences).
- A **path**belongs to one site and references specific endpoints via`endpoint_ids`.
- A **run**belongs to one path and records a single tool invocation.

The worker exposes a JSON REST API alongside the MCP endpoint.

Health check and service metadata.

**Response** `200`

Explore a website and capture its API endpoints.

**Request body**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | `string` | ✅ | Target URL to scout |
| `task` | `string` | ✅ | Natural-language description of what to find |

**Response** `200`

**Errors**

| Status | Body | When |
|---|---|---|
| `400` | `{"error": "Missing 'url' and 'task' in request body"}` | Required fields missing |
| `500` | `{"error": "..."}` | Browser, network, or storage failure |

Replay a scouted path — executes the captured API calls directly, no browser needed.

**Request body**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pathId` | `string` | ✅ | Path ID from a previous scout |
| `data` | `object` | Data to interpolate into the request |

**Response** `200`

**Errors**

| Status | Body | When |
|---|---|---|
| `400` | `{"error": "Missing 'pathId' in request body"}` | Required field missing |
| `500` | `{"error": "PathBrokenError: POST /api/v1/users returned 404"}` | Path is broken — call heal |
| `500` | `{"error": "..."}` | Network or storage failure |

Repair a broken path by retrying, then re-scouting if retries fail.

**Request body**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pathId` | `string` | ✅ | ID of the broken path |
| `error` | `string` | Description of what went wrong — helps the re-scout |

**Response** `200`

**Errors**

| Status | Body | When |
|---|---|---|
| `400` | `{"error": "Missing 'pathId' in request body"}` | Required field missing |
| `500` | `{"error": "..."}` | Browser, network, or storage failure |

Service metadata and directory route map.

**Response** `200`

List all domains in the directory. Requires `VECTORS` + `AI` bindings.

**Query parameters**

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `offset` | `integer` | `0` | Pagination offset |
| `limit` | `integer` | `20` | Max results to return |

**Response** `200`

Get the fingerprint (summary) for a domain.

**Response** `200` — Fingerprint object for the domain.

**Errors**

| Status | Body | When |
|---|---|---|
| `404` | `{"error": "NotFoundError: ..."}` | Domain not in directory |
| `503` | `{"error": "Directory not configured ..."}` | `VECTORS`/`AI`bindings missing |

Get the full OpenAPI 3.1 spec for a domain.

**Response** `200` — OpenAPI 3.1 JSON document.

Get the endpoints for a specific capability (e.g. `search`, `auth`, `crud`).

**Response** `200` — Capability slice with matching endpoints.

Get a single endpoint by method and path.

**Response** `200` — Endpoint detail object.

MCP (Streamable HTTP) endpoint. See [MCP Server guide](https://unsurf.coey.dev/guides/mcp) and [MCP Tools reference](https://unsurf.coey.dev/reference/tools).

All endpoints return permissive CORS headers (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`). `OPTIONS` preflight requests are handled automatically.

Any other method/path combination returns `404`:

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `bun run dev` | Local development via Alchemy |
| `bun run deploy` | Deploy to Cloudflare |
| `bun run generate` | Generate Drizzle migrations (internal dev workflow — not needed for deployment) |
| `bun run test` | Run test suite |
| `bun run check` | Lint and format (Biome) |
| `bun run typecheck` | TypeScript type checking |

# MCP Server | unsurf

Source: https://unsurf.coey.dev/guides/mcp

# MCP Server

The unsurf MCP server is available at:

It uses the **Streamable HTTP** transport from the [MCP specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io). The server runs in stateless mode — each request is independent.

For full documentation of all tool inputs, outputs, and error types, see the [MCP Tools reference](https://unsurf.coey.dev/reference/tools).

Add this to your Claude Desktop MCP config (`~/.claude/mcp.json`):

Restart Claude Desktop. You should see **unsurf** listed under the MCP tools icon.

Open Cursor Settings → MCP Servers → **Add Server** and enter:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | `unsurf` |
| Transport | `Streamable HTTP` |
| URL | `https://unsurf-api.coey.dev/mcp` |

Cursor will discover the available tools automatically.

Use the hosted MCP server for Cloudflare-side scout/search/plan work. Use the local stdio server when an agent should operate the Chrome session already open on your machine:

The local server exposes two tools:

- `unsurf_local_sessions`— list attachable local Chrome/CDP tabs
- `unsurf_local_execute`— run small browser action plans against the active attached browser, optionally recording an unsurf trace

This is the “browser is the auth” path: the tool does not mint credentials or create a new browser profile; it uses the session you already authenticated.

Any client that supports the Streamable HTTP transport can connect. Point it at the `/mcp` endpoint and send standard JSON-RPC messages:

The server supports the `initialize`, `tools/list`, and `tools/call` methods.

You can verify the MCP endpoint works with plain `curl`.

You should get back a response with `serverInfo` and `capabilities`.

The response lists the registered tools. The hosted server includes `scout`, `worker`, `heal`, `gallery`, `unsurf_search`, and `unsurf_execute`; `directory` and `agent-scout` appear when their optional bindings are configured.

Beyond the scout/worker/heal set, the MCP server exposes two tools that work with the record/observe/loop skills — a pair-pattern (search + execute) so agents have a small, stable surface to reason over:

List recorded traces. Filter by owner, task substring, or visibility. Returns `viewerUrl` values with grants pre-minted, ready to open.

Run one of unsurf’s Worker-safe skills. Today:

- `loopPlan`- `LoopSpec`from a natural-language goal via Kimi K2.6. Plan only; no browser drive. Feed the result to the local- `unsurf loop`CLI (or- `loop()`JS API) to actually record.

Actions that need local Node APIs (actual `record()` via agent-browser, `observeVideo()` via ffmpeg) are CLI-only until the cloud recording provider lands (Phase 4 in [NORTHSTAR.md](https://github.com/acoyfellow/unsurf/blob/main/docs/NORTHSTAR.md)).

When you deploy your own unsurf instance, the MCP endpoint is automatically available at `/mcp` on your worker URL.

-
Clone the repo and install dependencies:
-
Set the required environment variables (see [Configuration](https://unsurf.coey.dev/reference/config#environment-variables)):
-
Deploy:
-
Point your MCP clients at your worker URL:
